signals.entity: VivaBank (Viva.com) vs JCC Payment Systems Ltd
signals.signal: The Treasury of the Republic of Cyprus awarded the state electronic-payments contract to VivaBank Single-Member Banking Company S.A. (Viva.com), displacing JCC Payment Systems, the incumbent since 2010. Viva.com bid EUR 3.92m (part one) + EUR 172,942 (part two) against JCC's EUR 4.45m + EUR 522,821. Duration 67 months with two optional 12-month extensions; annual transaction value above EUR 1.5bn. Tender launched 07/01/2022; award to VivaBank 20/03/2026; JCC challenge filed 08/04/2026 and dismissed 15/07/2026. Implementation: 1 month technical preparation, 4-6 months connection to the Ariadne Payment Gateway, then 36 months of core transaction processing, covering cards and account-to-account payments for direct taxes, vehicle licences, social insurance and municipal charges via gov.cy.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail - Cyprus awards Viva.com EUR 1.5bn-a-year state payments contract
signals.implies: A Greek acquirer has taken the anchor public-sector payment flow off the Cypriot bank-owned processor. JCC must defend and re-platform its acquiring and digital-channel estate; Viva.com must stand up a Cyprus gateway integration in 2027. Both are POS/acquiring and managed-services openings for Printec.
signals.followup: Pull the award notice from eprocurement.gov.cy for the CPV codes and exact scope; identify which merchant/terminal estate migrates in 2027.

signals.entity: Treasury of the Republic of Cyprus / VivaBank
signals.signal: The Accountant-General reported that in H1-2026 bank transfers made up 85% of the total value of government receipts, online payments 10%, in-person electronic payments 1% and traditional methods 4%. Personal cheques have not been accepted since 01/01/2026; banker's drafts are to be withdrawn; cash is still accepted up to EUR 10,000. A EUR 4.1m contract with VivaBank Single-member Banking Company was signed on 12/08/2026, with implementation expected during 2027; the existing system, run by JCC Payment Systems Limited, processes about EUR 1.5bn annually.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail - Cyprus' government receives 85% of payments by bank transfer
signals.implies: Confirms the signature date (12/08/2026) and the EUR 4.1m headline for the Viva.com contract, and shows the state actively retiring paper instruments - a cash-automation and payment-acceptance modernisation window across public-sector counters.
signals.followup: Confirm whether physical cash desks at government counters are in scope for automation, which would open a Printec cash-recycler angle.

signals.signal: STATUS CHANGE on the 22/07/2026 baseline: the Eurobank Cyprus board has contracted from ~18 live vacancies to 8. The 10-role digital-channels/engineering cluster reported at 31/07 has largely disappeared or been filled. Only one new posting appeared in August - Project Manager, Nicosia, 20/08/2026. The remaining seven date 07-22/07/2026 and include 'Λειτουργός Διαχείρισης & Ανάπτυξης Ηλεκτρονικών Καναλιών' (Digital Channels Management & Development Officer, Nicosia, 21/07/2026), 'Associate Manager/Senior Quality Assurance Engineer' (13/07/2026) and 'Senior Project Manager' (07/07/2026).
signals.implies: The post-merger digital-channels build at Cyprus's second-largest bank has moved from recruiting into delivery, and project-management capacity is still being added. The window to supply tooling and managed services is now.
signals.followup: eurobank.cy remains Cloudflare-blocked to fetch; escalate to a browser session to confirm the official count and whether the cluster roles were filled or withdrawn.

signals.signal: Eurobank named Cyprus one of three core growth markets. Eurobank Limited operates 67 branches and business centres in Cyprus and contributed EUR 231m. Following the 2025 legal mergers (Hellenic Bank + Eurobank Cyprus, plus CNP insurance), operational integration is underway to create unified platforms; 15 sites still run a branch-in-branch model (8 ex-Eurobank, 7 ex-Hellenic) pending full network integration, and the bank has said combining systems, policies and processes could take up to two years with significant investment in branch renovation and digital platforms.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail - Eurobank highlights Cyprus role in regional growth plans
signals.implies: A live multi-year branch-transformation and platform-unification programme at a 67-branch network - directly addressable by Printec branch/self-service, cash automation and managed services.
signals.followup: Obtain the Eurobank H1-2026 results presentation for the Cyprus integration cost and capex line, and find the target date for retiring the branch-in-branch sites.

signals.signal: JCC's careers page shows 7 live vacancies (8 at 31/07/2026), 6 of them IT/infrastructure: Systems Engineer - Core Systems; Systems Engineer - Servers, Automation and Azure; Database Administrator; Technical Analyst - IT Business Applications; Support Engineer - Digital Channels; Manager Applications; plus one Call Center Agent. All Nicosia, under Technology Infrastructure and Digital. The page publishes no posting or closing dates.
signals.implies: JCC is running a sustained core-systems and Azure/automation build even as it loses the state contract - a re-platforming programme Printec can support with POS/acquiring, transaction monitoring and managed services.
signals.followup: Ask JCC whether the core-systems roles relate to digital-euro pilot readiness or to replacing lost state-payment volume.

signals.signal: CBC released its 'Payment Fraud Statistics: Second half of 2025' report on 25/08/2026. Payment fraud in Cyprus stayed relatively low against the euro-area average, but incidents are concentrated in online card payments and cross-border transactions, and Cyprus recorded the HIGHEST AVERAGE VALUE PER FRAUDULENT CREDIT TRANSFER of any euro-area country. Payment service users consistently bore the largest share of losses from credit-transfer fraud, unlike other payment instruments.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Payment Fraud Statistics: Second half of 2025
signals.implies: A regulator-published, quantified fraud gap on credit transfers in the same year instant payments went live - the strongest available hook for Printec transaction monitoring / fraud and AML-compliance tooling with Cypriot banks and PSPs.
signals.likelihood: High - VOP/instant-payment fraud controls are already a supervisory theme
signals.followup: Download the full report (EN and EL) and extract the per-instrument fraud values to build a bank-by-bank pitch.

signals.signal: From 03/08/2026 the CBC changed the licensing process for Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Institutions, adding a mandatory 'pre-application exploratory stage' with a non-refundable EUR 5,000 fee, and doubling the licensing application fee from EUR 5,000 to EUR 10,000. Part of the comprehensive licensing and supervisory strategy announced on 20/12/2024.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - New Licensing Process for Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Institutions
signals.implies: Higher barriers to entry consolidate payment volume among incumbent Cypriot PSPs and banks, and force applicants to demonstrate AML/compliance and operational readiness earlier - a pull for Printec AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring tooling at licence-stage.
signals.followup: Track how many EMI/PI applications enter the pre-application stage in Q4-2026 to size the addressable pipeline.

signals.signal: CBC published Tender 08/2026 for the purchase of services supporting ON-SITE INSPECTIONS of CBC-supervised institutions in relation to the Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Law of 2007 and its regulations and directives, for a period of THREE years. Announcement is Greek-only. A parallel Tender 15/2026 covers consultancy services for the CBC's Human Resources Directorate.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus - Προκήρυξη Διαγωνισμού 08/2026
signals.implies: The supervisor is outsourcing three years of AML on-site inspection support - evidence that AML examination intensity in Cyprus is rising, which pulls banks toward stronger AML/KYC and transaction-monitoring stacks.
signals.followup: Retrieve the Greek tender documents for the closing date and award, and check whether the award has been published on eprocurement.gov.cy.

signals.entity: Cyprus ATM estate (Central Bank of Cyprus data)
signals.signal: The Cypriot ATM network fell from 398 machines at end-2024 to 396 at end-2025. About 73% of Cypriot ATMs support contactless, versus roughly 38% across the euro area. EUR 2.6bn was withdrawn in H2-2025; withdrawal volumes fell while the average withdrawal rose 27% over three years, from EUR 307 (2022) to EUR 390 (2025). Banks have been placing new machines in remote areas while removing under-used units from central locations, and cashback at retail POS is growing as a complementary cash-access channel.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail - Cypriots withdraw EUR 2.6bn as local ATM network continues to shrink (citing Central Bank of Cyprus data)
signals.implies: A near-flat but actively re-sited 396-unit estate with high contactless penetration - the Cypriot ATM opportunity is refresh, recycling and redeployment rather than net expansion, plus cashback-at-POS enablement. Directly Printec ATM/self-service and cash automation.
signals.followup: Get the CBC Payment Statistics (22/07/2026) underlying table for the split of deposit-taking vs withdrawal-only ATMs, which would size the recycler opportunity.

signals.entity: Cyprus payment acceptance (ECB 2026 survey + CBC consumer survey)
signals.signal: Mobile payment acceptance by businesses jumped from 36% in 2024 to 68% in 2026, while card acceptance stayed broadly flat at 88% and cash acceptance was 92% across the euro area. Card payments make up 75% of all non-cash payment VOLUME in Cyprus - the highest share in the euro area - while credit transfers dominate by VALUE at 84%. A CBC survey of 506 respondents found 63% use cards weekly in physical shops and 23% pay weekly via internet/mobile banking; on the digital euro, 61% had no knowledge of it, 1% felt fully informed, 35% would use it daily and 28% are unlikely to adopt it.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail - Cash is still king as digital payments reshape Cyprus and Europe
signals.implies: Mobile acceptance nearly doubling in two years means a large Cypriot merchant estate is being re-terminalised or softPOS-enabled right now - a direct POS/acquiring and merchant-services opening, and the low digital-euro awareness flags a 2027 pilot communications and terminal-readiness workload.
signals.followup: Locate the underlying ECB SPACE/IPSOS 2026 acceptance dataset and the CBC consumer survey publication to cite primary numbers.
